In the given congruence, we have $a=268$ and $n=404$, and we're given that

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(268,404)=4.
$$

Since $b=16$ is divisible by $4,$ our congruence has $4$ solutions.

Next, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}268x & ≡16 &  & (\text{mod}\,404) \\ 4\cdot 67x & ≡4\cdot 4 &  & (\text{mod}\,4\cdot 101) \\ \cancel{4}\cdot 67x & ≡\cancel{4}\cdot 4 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{4}\cdot 101) \\ 67x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,101)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in this new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=67$ and ${n}_{1}=101$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(67,101)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $101.$

To find the solution, we must multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $67\,(\text{mod}\,101).$ To find the inverse of $67\,(\text{mod}\,101),$ we apply the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}101 & = & 67\cdot 1 & + & 34\, & ⇔ & \,34 & = & 101-67\cdot 1 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 67 & = & 34\cdot 1 & + & 33\, & ⇔ & \,33 & = & 67-34\cdot 1 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 34 & = & 33\cdot 1 & + & 1\, & ⇔ & \,1 & = & 34-33\cdot 1 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 33 & = & 33\cdot 1 & + & 0\, &  & \, &  & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, back-substituting in the usual way gives the following:

$$
1=2\cdot 101-3\cdot 67
$$

We can write this result in modulo $101,$ as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot 101-3\cdot 67 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,101) \\ -3\cdot 67 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,101) \\ (101-3)\cdot 67 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,101) \\ 98\cdot 67 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,101)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse of $67$ modulo $101$ is $98.$

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $98,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}67x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,101) \\ 98\cdot 67x & ≡98\cdot 4 &  & (\text{mod}\,101) \\ x & ≡392 &  & (\text{mod}\,101) \\ x & ≡101\cdot 3+89 &  & (\text{mod}\,101) \\ x & ≡89 &  & (\text{mod}\,101)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡89\,(\text{mod}\,101).$

But our original congruence was modulo $404$ (not modulo $101$). To find all the solutions modulo $404,$ we repeatedly add $101$ to $89$ modulo $404$ until we reach the number $89$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡89 &  & (\text{mod}\,404) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡89+101≡190 &  & (\text{mod}\,404) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡190+101≡291 &  & (\text{mod}\,404) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡291+101≡392 &  & (\text{mod}\,404) \\ {x}_{5} & ≡392+101≡493≡404+89≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,404)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1,2,3,4}≡89,\,190,\,291,\,392\,(\text{mod}\,404).
$$
